bibliographic.title: Performance of large language models as an information resource on functional hypothalamic amenorrhea for patients and healthcare professionals
bibliographic.authors: Nancy Safwan, Jana Karam, Sarah L. Berga, Maria D. Hurtado Andrade, Kristin Cole, Stacey J. Winham, Stephanie S. Faubion, Chrisandra L. Shufelt
bibliographic.citation_apa: Safwan, N., Karam, J., Berga, S. L., Hurtado Andrade, M. D., Cole, K., Winham, S. J., Faubion, S. S., & Shufelt, C. L. (2026). Performance of large language models as an information resource on functional hypothalamic amenorrhea for patients and healthcare professionals. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 9, 1788928. https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2026.1788928

methodology.method_family: comparative performance evaluation with expert blinded rating
methodology.study_design: cross-sectional comparative evaluation of LLM-generated answers to predefined clinical and patient questions
methodology.sample_description: 11 patient-level and 15 clinician-level FHA-related questions entered into four LLMs; responses rated by three blinded expert reviewers with a fourth resolving discordant scores
methodology.technology_context: ChatGPT 3.5, ChatGPT 4.0, Gemini, and OpenEvidence used to answer FHA-related questions for patients and healthcare professionals

eligibility.decision_rationale: The study is an empirical healthcare LLM accuracy and readability evaluation in a regulated clinical domain, with blinded expert human review of outputs and a discussion mention of human-in-the-loop feedback. The provided text does not study conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, accountability frameworks, audit/logging, compliance controls, or post-deployment governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front-matter and partial abstract/introduction text were supplied; full-text verification is needed to confirm whether governance, oversight, safety, or accountability content appears beyond performance evaluation.

appraisal.notes: Methods are clearly described for a comparative LLM benchmarking study with blinded expert adjudication and statistical comparison. Ethics, full limitations, and broader governance implications are not evident in the supplied excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: The study is internally coherent for evaluating LLM answer accuracy and readability in a healthcare context, but its direct relevance to conversational governance is limited because the supplied text centers on clinical information quality rather than governance architecture, compliance, or operational controls.

coding.theme: Human expert evaluation of LLM medical information quality
coding.subtheme: Post-hoc human review and proposed human-in-the-loop improvement in clinical LLM use

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs showed generally good but variable performance in answering FHA-related questions for patients and clinicians, with model differences in accuracy and readability and a recommendation that human-in-the-loop feedback may improve accuracy.
synthesis.contribution: Provides empirical comparative evidence on LLM answer quality in a regulated healthcare setting and demonstrates a blinded multi-reviewer human evaluation workflow for LLM outputs.
synthesis.limitations: Based on a small fixed question set for one medical condition; supplied text indicates incorrect or incomplete information still occurred; broader governance implications are not developed in the provided excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as borderline supporting evidence on human expert review and human-in-the-loop improvement in regulated healthcare LLM use, not as central evidence on conversational governance frameworks.

evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed original research article in Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 2026.
evidence.excerpt: TYPE Original Research PUBLISHED 15 June 2026 DOI 10.3389/frai.2026.1788928

evidence.claim: Study objective is comparative evaluation of LLM accuracy, readability, and overall performance for FHA questions.
evidence.excerpt: To assess and compare the accuracy, readability, and overall performance of large language models (LLMs) in answering questions about functional hypothalamic amenorrhea (FHA) for patients and healthcare professionals.

evidence.claim: Empirical design uses predefined patient and clinician questions across four named LLMs.
evidence.excerpt: A total of 11 patient-level and 15 clinician-level FHA-related questions were entered separately into four LLMs: ChatGPT 3.5 (free version), ChatGPT 4.0 (updated, paid subscription), Gemini, and OpenEvidence.

evidence.claim: Human expert oversight is implemented through blinded review and discordance resolution.
evidence.excerpt: Responses were evaluated by three expert reviewers blinded to the LLM used who rated them as accurate and complete, accurate but incomplete, or inaccurate. A fourth reviewer resolved discordant scores.

evidence.claim: Results report comparative accuracy across models.
evidence.excerpt: For patient-level questions, ChatGPT 4.0 achieved the highest accuracy (9 of 11; 82%), followed by ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini (each 8 of 11; 73%)

evidence.claim: Discussion notes residual errors and suggests human-in-the-loop feedback.
evidence.excerpt: LLMs demonstrated good overall performance in answering FHA-related questions but often provided incorrect or incomplete information. Fine tuning field-specific data, engineered prompts, and obtaining human-in-the-loop feedback may help improve the accuracy

evidence.claim: LLMs are framed as generative AI tools emerging in healthcare.
evidence.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs), a form of generative artificial intelligence (AI), are rapidly emerging as transformative tools in healthcare
Accuracy and completeness were compared using odds ratios (95% CI) with ChatGPT 3.5 as the reference model, and differences in readability were analyzed using Friedman's test.

evidence.claim: No conversational governance framework is described in the supplied text.
evidence.excerpt: To assess and compare the accuracy, readability, and overall performance of large language models (LLMs)
